lesson_scope: Comprehensive cross-topic synthesis of logarithmic and exponential functions with calculus, trigonometry, partial fractions, differential equations, and numerical analysis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Logarithmic equation quadratic resolution.

walkthrough.text:
Rewrite using logarithm power law:
$$\ln\left((x - 1)^2\right) = \ln(3x + 1) \implies (x - 1)^2 = 3x + 1$$

Expand and solve the quadratic equation:
$$x^2 - 2x + 1 = 3x + 1 \implies x^2 - 5x = 0 \implies x(x - 5) = 0$$
$$\text{Since } x > 1, \; x = 5$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Exponential linear integration by parts.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exponential linear integration by parts.

walkthrough.text:
Integrate by parts with $u = x$ and $v' = \mathrm{e}^{2x}$:
$$\int x\mathrm{e}^{2x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{1}{2}x\mathrm{e}^{2x} - \int \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{2x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{1}{2}x\mathrm{e}^{2x} - \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{2x}$$

Substitute limits $0$ and $1$:
$$\left[\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{2x}(2x - 1)\right]_0^1 = \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^2(1) - \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^0(-1) = \frac{\mathrm{e}^2 + 1}{4}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Trigonometric integral producing exact logarithm.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Trigonometric integral producing exact logarithm.

hints: Antiderivative of $\tan x$ is $\ln|\sec x|$ or $-\ln|\cos x|$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the standard integral for tangent:
$$\int_0^{\pi/4} \tan x\,\mathrm{d}x = \left[\ln|\sec x|\right]_0^{\pi/4}$$

Substitute limits:
$$= \ln(\sec(\pi/4)) - \ln(\sec 0) = \ln(\sqrt{2}) - \ln(1) = \frac{1}{2}\ln 2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Separable ODE with exponential solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Separable ODE with exponential solution.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int 2x\,\mathrm{d}x \implies \ln y = x^2 + c$$

Apply initial condition $y(0) = 3$:
$$\ln 3 = 0 + c \implies c = \ln 3 \implies \ln y = x^2 + \ln 3 \implies y = 3\mathrm{e}^{x^2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exponential-trigonometric product differentiation.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate using the product rule:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = (3\mathrm{e}^{3x})\cos(2x) + \mathrm{e}^{3x}(-2\sin(2x)) = \mathrm{e}^{3x}(3\cos(2x) - 2\sin(2x))$$

Evaluate at $x = 0$:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\Big|_{x=0} = \mathrm{e}^0(3\cos 0 - 2\sin 0) = 1(3(1) - 0) = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Exponential power equation exact logarithmic form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exponential power equation exact logarithmic form.

walkthrough.text:
Take natural logarithms of both sides:
$$(2x - 1)\ln 3 = (x + 2)\ln 5$$

Expand and collect terms involving $x$ on one side:
$$2x\ln 3 - x\ln 5 = \ln 3 + 2\ln 5 \implies x(2\ln 3 - \ln 5) = \ln 3 + 2\ln 5$$

Combine logarithms using power and product laws:
$$x = \frac{\ln 3 + \ln(5^2)}{\ln(3^2) - \ln 5} = \frac{\ln(3 \times 25)}{\ln(9/5)} = \frac{\ln 75}{\ln(9/5)}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Stationary point of polynomial-exponential product.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Stationary point of polynomial-exponential product.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate using the product rule:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x\mathrm{e}^{-x} + x^2(-\mathrm{e}^{-x}) = (2x - x^2)\mathrm{e}^{-x} = x(2 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-x}$$

Set the derivative to zero for non-zero $x$:
$$2 - x = 0 \implies x = 2$$
$$y(2) = 2^2 \mathrm{e}^{-2} = 4\mathrm{e}^{-2} \implies \left(2, 4\mathrm{e}^{-2}\right)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies product rule: $2x\mathrm{e}^{-x} - x^2\mathrm{e}^{-x} = x(2 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-x}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Repeated integration by parts for bounded area.

walkthrough.text:
Integrate by parts twice:
$$\int x^2 \mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -x^2\mathrm{e}^{-x} + \int 2x\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -x^2\mathrm{e}^{-x} - 2x\mathrm{e}^{-x} - 2\mathrm{e}^{-x} = -(x^2 + 2x + 2)\mathrm{e}^{-x}$$

Evaluate between limits $0$ and $2$:
$$A = \left[-(2^2 + 2(2) + 2)\mathrm{e}^{-2}\right] - \left[-(0 + 0 + 2)\mathrm{e}^0\right] = -10\mathrm{e}^{-2} - (-2) = 2 - 10\mathrm{e}^{-2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Separable ODE with partial fraction integration.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Separable ODE with partial fraction integration.

walkthrough.text:
Decompose into partial fractions:
$$\frac{1}{x(x + 1)} = \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{x + 1}$$

Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{y + 1}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \left(\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{x + 1}\right)\mathrm{d}x \implies \ln(y + 1) = \ln\left(\frac{x}{x + 1}\right) + C$$

Apply initial condition $(1, 1)$:
$$\ln(2) = \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + C \implies C = \ln 4$$
$$\ln(y + 1) = \ln\left(\frac{4x}{x + 1}\right) \implies y + 1 = \frac{4x}{x + 1} \implies y = \frac{4x - (x + 1)}{x + 1} = \frac{3x - 1}{x + 1}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Particular value and asymptotic limit calculation.

hints: As $x \to \infty$, divide numerator and denominator by $x$: $\frac{3 - 1/x}{1 + 1/x} \to 3$.

walkthrough.text:
Solve for $x$ when $y = 2$:
$$\frac{3x - 1}{x + 1} = 2 \implies 3x - 1 = 2x + 2 \implies x = 3$$

Evaluate the asymptotic limit as $x \to \infty$:
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} y = \lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{3 - \frac{1}{x}}{1 + \frac{1}{x}} = \frac{3 - 0}{1 + 0} = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Stationary point exact coordinates for logarithmic quotient.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Stationary point exact coordinates for logarithmic quotient.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate using the quotient rule:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \frac{\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)(x^2) - \ln(3x)(2x)}{x^4} = \frac{x - 2x\ln(3x)}{x^4} = \frac{1 - 2\ln(3x)}{x^3}$$

Set the derivative to zero to find the stationary coordinates:
$$1 - 2\ln(3x) = 0 \implies \ln(3x) = \frac{1}{2} \implies 3x = \mathrm{e}^{1/2} \implies x = \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}}{3}$$
$$y = \frac{\ln\left(3 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}}{3}\right)}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}}{3}\right)^2} = \frac{1/2}{\mathrm{e}/9} = \frac{9}{2\mathrm{e}}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Normal line exact fraction derivation.

walkthrough.text:
Find the $y$-coordinate and tangent gradient at $x = \frac{1}{3}$:
$$y\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{\ln(3(1/3))}{(1/3)^2} = \frac{\ln 1}{1/9} = 0 \implies \left(\frac{1}{3}, 0\right)$$
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = \frac{1 - 2\ln(3(1/3))}{(1/3)^3} = \frac{1 - 2(0)}{1/27} = 27$$

Compute the normal gradient and write the line equation:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\frac{1}{27}$$
$$y - 0 = -\frac{1}{27}\left(x - \frac{1}{3}\right) \implies y = -\frac{1}{27}x + \frac{1}{81}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms normal equation: $m_N = -\frac{1}{27} \implies y - 0 = -\frac{1}{27}(x - 1/3) \implies y = -\frac{1}{27}x + \frac{1}{81}$ (or with $m_T = 27$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Exponential parameter identification from data points.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exponential parameter identification from data points.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute given data into the model:
$$A k^1 = 12 \quad \text{and} \quad A k^3 = 48$$

Divide the second equation by the first:
$$\frac{A k^3}{A k} = \frac{48}{12} \implies k^2 = 4 \implies k = 2 \quad (k > 0)$$

Substitute $k = 2$ back to find $A$:
$$A(2) = 12 \implies A = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up equations: $A k = 12$ and $A k^3 = 48$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Model constraint rearrangement and numerical iteration.

hints: Evaluate $f(3.5) < 0$ and $f(4.0) > 0$ to confirm root in $[3.5, 4.0]$.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange the constraint equation:
$$6(2^t) = 100 - t^2 \implies 2^t = \frac{100 - t^2}{6} \implies t\ln 2 = \ln\left(\frac{100 - t^2}{6}\right) \implies t = \frac{\ln\left(\frac{100 - t^2}{6}\right)}{\ln 2}$$

Perform iterative calculations starting from $t_1 = 3.8$:
$$t_2 = \frac{\ln\left(\frac{100 - 3.8^2}{6}\right)}{\ln 2} = \frac{\ln(14.2600)}{\ln 2} = 3.8339$$
$$t_3 = \frac{\ln\left(\frac{100 - 3.8339^2}{6}\right)}{\ln 2} = \frac{\ln(14.2169)}{\ln 2} = 3.8296$$
$$t_4 = 3.8301, \quad t_5 = 3.8301 \implies t = 3.82 \text{ (or } 3.83 \text{)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges $2^t = \frac{100 - t^2}{6} \implies t\ln 2 = \ln\left(\frac{100 - t^2}{6}\right) \implies t = \frac{\ln((100 - t^2)/6)}{\ln 2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Surd exponential product stationary maximum.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Surd exponential product stationary maximum.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate using the product rule:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right)\mathrm{e}^{-x/2} + \sqrt{x}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}\right)$$

Factorize over a common denominator:
$$= \frac{\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}}{2\sqrt{x}} - \frac{x\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{(1 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}}{2\sqrt{x}}$$

Set the numerator to zero to obtain the maximum point:
$$1 - x = 0 \implies x = 1$$
$$y(1) = \sqrt{1}\mathrm{e}^{-1/2} = \mathrm{e}^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}} \implies \left(1, \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}}\right)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Combines over common denominator $2\sqrt{x}$ to get $\frac{(1 - x)\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}}{2\sqrt{x}}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Volume of revolution via integration by parts.

walkthrough.text:
Square the curve function to set up the volume of revolution:
$$y^2 = \left(\sqrt{x}\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}\right)^2 = x\mathrm{e}^{-x}$$
$$V = \pi \int_0^2 x\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate by parts with $u = x$ and $v' = \mathrm{e}^{-x}$:
$$\int x\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -x\mathrm{e}^{-x} - \int -\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -x\mathrm{e}^{-x} - \mathrm{e}^{-x} = -(x + 1)\mathrm{e}^{-x}$$

Evaluate across limits $0$ to $2$:
$$V = \pi \left[-(2 + 1)\mathrm{e}^{-2} - (-(0 + 1)\mathrm{e}^0)\right] = \pi \left(-3\mathrm{e}^{-2} + 1\right) = \pi(1 - 3\mathrm{e}^{-2})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up volume integral: $V = \pi \int_0^2 y^2\,\mathrm{d}x = \pi \int_0^2 x\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Logistic growth ODE partial fraction solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Logistic growth ODE partial fraction solution.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{N(200 - N)}{4000} \implies \int \frac{200}{N(200 - N)}\,\mathrm{d}N = \int \frac{1}{20}\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Split into partial fractions and integrate:
$$\frac{200}{N(200 - N)} = \frac{1}{N} + \frac{1}{200 - N}$$
$$\ln N - \ln(200 - N) = \frac{t}{20} + C \implies \ln\left(\frac{N}{200 - N}\right) = \frac{t}{20} + C$$

Apply initial condition $N(0) = 40$:
$$\ln\left(\frac{40}{160}\right) = 0 + C \implies C = \ln\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = -\ln 4$$
$$\ln\left(\frac{N}{200 - N}\right) = \frac{t}{20} - \ln 4 \implies \frac{N}{200 - N} = \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{t/20}$$
$$\frac{200 - N}{N} = 4\mathrm{e}^{-t/20} \implies \frac{200}{N} - 1 = 4\mathrm{e}^{-t/20} \implies N = \frac{200}{1 + 4\mathrm{e}^{-t/20}}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Decomposes into partial fractions: $\int \left(\frac{1}{N} + \frac{1}{200 - N}\right)\mathrm{d}N \implies \ln\left(\frac{N}{200 - N}\right) = \frac{t}{20} + C$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exact logarithmic time and growth rate evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Find the time when $N = 100$:
$$100 = \frac{200}{1 + 4\mathrm{e}^{-t/20}} \implies 1 + 4\mathrm{e}^{-t/20} = 2 \implies 4\mathrm{e}^{-t/20} = 1$$
$$\mathrm{e}^{t/20} = 4 \implies \frac{t}{20} = \ln 4 \implies t = 20\ln 4 = 40\ln 2$$

Calculate the growth rate directly from the differential equation:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{1}{20}(100)\left(1 - \frac{100}{200}\right) = 5\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = 5\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 2.5$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Normal line and stationary point synthesis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Normal line and stationary point synthesis.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate using the product rule:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = (1)\mathrm{e}^{-x} + (x + 2)(-\mathrm{e}^{-x}) = -(x + 1)\mathrm{e}^{-x}$$

Find the normal line at $(0, 2)$:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -(0 + 1)\mathrm{e}^0 = -1 \implies m_{\text{normal}} = 1$$
$$y - 2 = 1(x - 0) \implies y = x + 2$$

Locate the stationary point:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0 \implies -(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = -1$$
$$y(-1) = (-1 + 2)\mathrm{e}^{-(-1)} = 1 \cdot \mathrm{e}^1 = \mathrm{e} \implies (-1, \mathrm{e})$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculus area formula linked to transcendental fixed-point iteration.

walkthrough.text:
Integrate by parts to find the area function $A(p)$:
$$A(p) = \int_0^p (x + 2)\mathrm{e}^{-x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \left[-(x + 2)\mathrm{e}^{-x} - \mathrm{e}^{-x}\right]_0^p = \left[-(x + 3)\mathrm{e}^{-x}\right]_0^p$$
$$= -(p + 3)\mathrm{e}^{-p} - (-(3)\mathrm{e}^0) = 3 - (p + 3)\mathrm{e}^{-p}$$

Equate $A(p) = 2.5$ and rearrange:
$$3 - (p + 3)\mathrm{e}^{-p} = 2.5 \implies (p + 3)\mathrm{e}^{-p} = 0.5 \implies \mathrm{e}^p = 2(p + 3) = 2p + 6$$
$$p = \ln(2p + 6)$$
